summary: Switch between sibling views of the same object.

pairs.dont: Use tabs to move between different objects, or as page navigation.
pairs.do: Use them for views of one object — an endpoint's Overview, Trunks, Alerts.
pairs.why: Tabs promise you are still looking at the same thing. Break that and people lose track of what they are on.

pairs.dont: Use a segmented control for page-level sections.
pairs.do: Underline for page sections, Minimal inside a card or drawer, Brand/Gray/Border for compact toggles.
pairs.why: The file assigns each type a place. Segmented styles read as a control; underline reads as structure.

pairs.dont: Cram nine long labels into a horizontal row.
pairs.do: Switch to Line tabs past about six sections, or when labels are long.
pairs.why: Horizontal tabs that wrap or scroll hide their own options, which defeats the point of showing them all.

pairs.dont: Use tabs for a sequence someone must complete in order.
pairs.do: Use Stepper for order, tabs for free movement.
pairs.why: Tabs say "look wherever you like". A sequence needs to say "finish this first".

pairs.dont: Let the panel resize the page as you move between tabs.
pairs.do: Give the panel a stable minimum height where the content varies.
pairs.why: The tabs move under the pointer if the page reflows, and the next click lands on the wrong one.

a11y: Radix supplies the tablist, tab and tabpanel roles and arrow-key movement between tabs.
The panel is focusable and carries its own ring, so keyboard users reach the content after the tab strip rather than tabbing through every tab first.
